hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

paper.title: Apolipoprotein E aggregation in microglia initiates Alzheimer's disease pathology by seeding β-amyloidosis.

findings.finding_description: APOE aggregates were purified from human AD cortex autopsies (2% sarkosyl insolubility, anti-hAPOE immunopurification, then Aβ immunodepletion). Negative-stain EM showed APOE-immunogold-positive, wavy snake-like fibrils in both APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 cases. No quantitative APOE4 vs APOE3 comparison of aggregation is reported, and no endo-lysosomal localization is assessed. The tissue is AD and aged, so this falls outside the hypothesis population; it bears only weakly on the hypothesis.
findings.quote: We detected APOE but only minimal amounts of Aβ, and negative staining revealed wavy snake-like fibrillar morphology of the isolated aggregates obtained from both APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 AD autopsies, as observed in mice, which were positive for APOE immune-gold labeling
findings.summary: Fibrillar APOE aggregates were isolated from both APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 human AD brains, with no genotype difference in amount reported and no endo-lysosomal readout.
findings.experimental_system: Human AD brain autopsy cortex (APOE3/3 and APOE4/4), sarkosyl-insoluble immunopurified fractions
findings.needs_review: directness corrected 1/5 -> 3/4: no APOE4-vs-3 comparison and no endo-lysosomal localization

findings.finding_description: Microglia were co-treated in culture with lipidated APOE3 or APOE4 particles plus Aβ-42, and β-sheet (MX04+) aggregates and TMR-cholesterol transfer were quantified. APOE4 induced more MX04+ aggregates and transferred more TMR-cholesterol into cells than APOE3. Aggregation was read out with MX04 rather than as APOE aggregation localized to the endo-lysosome, the species of the cells is not stated in this excerpt, and Aβ-42 was co-applied.
findings.quote: Next, we carried out the experiments using lipidated APOE3 and APOE4 and found that APOE4 was more efficient in inducing MX04+ aggregates and in transferring TMR-cholesterol into the cells compared with APOE3 (Figures S7G–S7I).
findings.summary: Lipidated APOE4 induced more MX04+ (APOE/Aβ) aggregates in cultured microglia than APOE3.
findings.experimental_system: cultured microglia (likely primary mouse or BV2; not specified in excerpt) treated with recombinant lipidated APOE3/APOE4 plus Aβ-42

findings.finding_description: Recombinant APOE plus fluorophore-coupled Aβ-42 induced concentration-dependent MX04+ aggregates positive for APOE and Aβ in BV2 cells. Similar aggregates formed in primary microglia and human iPSC-derived microglia but not in primary astrocytes. No isoform comparison was made, so this only shows the cell-type specificity of APOE aggregation, including in human iPSC microglia.
findings.quote: Similar results were observed in primary microglia and human iPSC-derived microglia (Figures 5B, S6B, and S6C), but not with primary astrocytes (Figures S6D and S6E).
findings.summary: APOE-induced MX04+ aggregates formed in microglia, including human iPSC microglia, but not in astrocytes; no isoform comparison.
findings.experimental_system: BV2 cells, primary microglia, human iPSC-derived microglia, primary astrocytes treated with recombinant APOE + Aβ-42

findings.finding_description: Inhibiting lysosomal degradation (Lys05/chloroquine, bafilomycin, leupeptin) increased APOE/Aβ-42-induced MX04+ aggregate formation in microglia. This implicates the endo-lysosomal compartment in APOE aggregation. Class 5 because the APOE isoform was not varied, so the hypothesis cause is not tested.
findings.quote: When microglia were treated with compounds that interfere with lysosomal degradation (Lys05/chloroquine, bafilomycin, or leupeptin), we detected increased MX04+ aggregate formation (Figures 5C, 5D, S6H, and S6I).
findings.summary: Lysosomal dysfunction increases APOE-induced aggregation in microglia, supporting an endo-lysosomal site; no isoform comparison.
findings.experimental_system: BV2 / microglia in culture treated with APOE + Aβ-42

findings.finding_description: After uptake of APOE-Halo lipoprotein particles by microglia, density gradient centrifugation showed that most APOE-Halo was recovered in the unlipidated fraction. This is consistent with intracellular delipidation producing aggregation-prone species. Class 5 because no isoform comparison was made and aggregation was not measured directly.
findings.quote: Subsequently, we utilized a biochemical approach involving density gradient centrifugation to separate lipidated from unlipidated APOE-Halo and observed that the majority of APOE-Halo was recovered from the unlipidated fraction in cell extracts (Figure S7F).
findings.summary: Internalized APOE becomes largely delipidated in microglia, a proposed precursor to endo-lysosomal aggregation.
findings.experimental_system: primary microglia cultures treated with APOE-Halo lipoprotein particles

findings.finding_description: BV2 microglia made deficient for squalene synthase (Fdft1) by CRISPR-Cas9 were treated with lipidated APOE plus Aβ-42. They formed more MX04+ (β-sheet dye) aggregates than control BV2 cells. Directness class 5: no APOE4 vs APOE3 comparison was made, the cells are a mouse microglial line rather than human brain cells, and aggregation was co-treated with Aβ and was not localized specifically to the endo-lysosome in this panel. It bears on the hypothesis only as context that cellular APOE aggregation can be modulated.
findings.quote: Notably, treatment with lipidated APOE and Aβ-42 was associated with an increase in MX04+ aggregate formation in Fdft1-deficient BV2 as compared with control cells (Figure 7F).
findings.summary: Blocking cholesterol synthesis in BV2 microglia increased MX04+ aggregate formation after APOE/Aβ-42 treatment; APOE isoforms were not compared.
findings.experimental_system: Fdft1-deficient (CRISPR) BV2 mouse microglial cell line treated with lipidated APOE and Aβ-42

findings.finding_description: 5xFAD mice with microglia-specific Fdft1 knockout (CX3CR1CreERT2) were examined at 3.5 months. They had more microglia containing MX04+ fibrillary material within the lysosomal compartment than 5xFAD controls. Directness class 5: there was no APOE4 vs APOE3 genotype comparison, the system is an in vivo mouse AD model rather than non-AD human cells, and the MX04+ material was not shown to be APOE specifically.
findings.quote: In addition, we detected enhanced numbers of microglia with MX04+ fibrillary morphology within the lysosomal compartment following cholesterol synthesis ablation (Figure 7G)
findings.summary: Microglial cholesterol-synthesis ablation in 5xFAD mice increased lysosomal MX04+ fibrillary material in microglia; APOE isoforms were not compared.
findings.experimental_system: CX3CR1CreERT2 Fdft1flox/flox 5xFAD mouse microglia in vivo

findings.finding_description: Recombinant APOE4 incubated at 37°C for up to 4 weeks formed aggregates (higher-molecular-weight FPLC fractions, Thioflavin T fluorescence, reduced α-helicity), whereas APOE3 analyzed in parallel showed none of these aggregation-associated changes.
findings.quote: When APOE3 was analyzed similarly, we did not observe altered ϴ222/ϴ208 ratio, increase in Thioflavin T fluorescence intensity, or drastic changes in molecular weight determined by FPLC (Figures 3E and S4G).
findings.summary: In a cell-free system, APOE4 aggregates but APOE3 does not.
findings.experimental_system: recombinant human APOE3 and APOE4 in cell-free buffer at 37°C

findings.finding_description: In an RT-QuIC assay in which monomeric Aβ was co-incubated with three-week pre-incubated recombinant APOE3 or APOE4, Aβ aggregation was accelerated more strongly by APOE4 than by APOE3.
findings.quote: Co-incubating Aβ with 3-week preincubated recombinant hAPOE accelerated Aβ aggregation with APOE4 having a stronger effect on Aβ aggregation compared with APOE3 (Figure 3F).
findings.summary: APOE4 drives Aβ aggregation more strongly than APOE3 in vitro.
findings.experimental_system: recombinant human APOE3/APOE4 with monomeric Aβ in RT-QuIC

findings.finding_description: When pre-incubated recombinant APOE4 aggregates were injected into 5xFAD mice, MX04+ amyloid plaques increased significantly; recombinant APOE3 prepared under the same conditions did not increase plaque number.
findings.quote: Injection of recombinant APOE3, prepared via a 3-week preincubation, did not result in an increase in the number of MX04+ amyloid plaques in the seeding experiment (Figure 3G).
findings.summary: Only APOE4 recombinant aggregates seed Aβ plaques in vivo; APOE3 does not.
findings.experimental_system: 5xFAD mice injected with recombinant human APOE3 or APOE4 aggregates

findings.finding_description: When APOE3 and APOE4 were prepared as lipidated particles, no aggregation was detected in the cell-free aggregation assay, indicating lipidation inhibits aggregation for both isoforms.
findings.quote: Notably, when the assay was performed with APOE3 and APOE4 prepared as lipidated particles, no aggregation was detected indicating that lipidation hampers aggregation in cell-free environment (Figures S4G and S4H).
findings.summary: Lipidation blocks both APOE3 and APOE4 aggregation in vitro.
findings.experimental_system: recombinant lipidated human APOE3 and APOE4 particles in cell-free buffer

findings.finding_description: 5xFAD mice carrying the human APOE4 knock-in allele had a higher MX04+ amyloid plaque load than 5xFAD APOE3 knock-in mice.
findings.quote: First, we compared MX04+ amyloid plaque number and detected a higher MX04+ plaque load in 5xFAD APOE4 KI compared with 5xFAD APOE3 KI and 5xFAD mice (Figures 3A, S4A, and S4B).
findings.summary: APOE4 increases Aβ plaque load in humanized 5xFAD mice.
findings.experimental_system: 5xFAD APOE3 knock-in and 5xFAD APOE4 knock-in mice in vivo

findings.finding_description: When immunopurified APOE aggregates from the same AD patient were injected into 5xFAD APOE3 or APOE4 knock-in mice, plaque numbers were elevated in both lines but higher counts were observed in 5xFAD APOE4 KI recipients.
findings.quote: Subsequently, we injected the same immunopurified APOE aggregates from an AD patient into either 5xFAD APOE3 KI or 5xFAD APOE4 KI mice and observed that APOE aggregate injections increased amyloid plaque numbers compared with control injections in both mouse lines, with higher MX04+ plaque counts observed in 5xFAD APOE4 KI mice (Figure 3C).
findings.summary: The APOE4 genotype augments seeded plaque formation even when the seed is the same human APOE aggregate.
findings.experimental_system: 5xFAD APOE3 or APOE4 knock-in mice injected with human AD-derived APOE aggregates

findings.finding_description: Immunopurified APOE aggregates prepared from both APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 AD patient brains enhanced MX04+ plaque formation when injected into 5xFAD mice.
findings.quote: We injected immunopurified APOE3 and APOE4 aggregates into 5xFAD mice and found that both were able to enhance MX04+ plaque formation as compared with control injections (Figures 3B and S4C).
findings.summary: Both human APOE3 and APOE4 aggregates seed plaques in vivo.
findings.experimental_system: 5xFAD mice injected with immunopurified human APOE3 or APOE4 aggregates from AD patients

findings.finding_description: Sarkosyl-insoluble APOE aggregates isolated from both APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 AD autopsy cortices displayed wavy fibrillar morphology by negative staining, similar to aggregates from mice.
findings.quote: We detected APOE but only minimal amounts of Aβ, and negative staining revealed wavy snake-like fibrillar morphology of the isolated aggregates obtained from both APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 AD autopsies, as observed in mice, which were positive for APOE immune-gold labeling (Figures 2B and S2G).
findings.summary: Both APOE3 and APOE4 AD brains contain fibrillar APOE aggregates.
findings.experimental_system: sarkosyl-insoluble fractions from APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 human AD autopsy cortex
findings.needs_review: directness corrected 1/5 -> 3/4: no APOE4-vs-3 comparison and no endo-lysosomal localization

findings.finding_description: In 5xFAD ApoE-Halo mice, intracellular APOE-Halo+MX04+ aggregates within IBA1+ microglia were frequently associated with CD68, a marker of endosomal/lysosomal compartments.
findings.quote: APOE-Halo+MX04+ structures inside of IBA1+ cells were often associated with CD68, a marker for endosomal/lysosomal compartment of activated microglia (Figures 4A, 4C, S5A, and S5B).
findings.summary: APOE aggregates localize to microglial endo-lysosomes in an AD mouse model.
findings.experimental_system: 5xFAD ApoE-Halo mouse brain microglia in vivo

findings.finding_description: Intracellular MX04+ aggregates inside microglia were not specific to mouse AD models; they were also detected in human AD autopsy brain tissue.
findings.quote: Intracellular MX04+ aggregates within microglia were not specific to the 5xFAD AD model, as we detected these in two additional mouse models of AD (APP/PS1 and NL-G-F mice) (Figure 4C), as well as in human autopsy samples (Figures 4D and S5C).
findings.summary: Microglial APOE/Aβ aggregates are also present in human AD brain.
